s5.2 evaluation-harness smoke, attempt 1. Completed both tool-calling generation passes and scored the first one (composite 0.5319 at 40 items per category, a sample size too small to be a baseline), then raised while writing the second pass's per-item file: one completion in 378 wrote a Python set literal where a number belongs, and the parser handed the set straight to the artifact writer. Both raw completion files were already saved, which is the design working as intended; the fix was verified against all 378 of them locally at no compute cost. Charged in full because it spent real GPU time and produced the template-mode and surface-form evidence the smoke was written to get.

s5.2 evaluation-harness smoke, attempt 2, narrowed to the three components attempt 1 never reached. COMPLETE with 0 assertion failures: structured output, instruction following and the probe set with its clean control arm all generated, scored and saved. 27,054 generated tokens at 247.2 tok/s. Instruction following read 0.800 prompt-level at n=40 against a published 86.23 for this checkpoint, which is the harness landing where it should. Two silent artifact bugs found by reading what came back: a basename collision that replaced raw completions with scored files, and a summary that logged as saved and was not retrievable. The first was fixed here; the second was misdiagnosed as a .json-versus-.jsonl problem and the real cause was only found on c644aac2, recorded there.

s5.2 competitor smoke at 40 items per category on ibm-granite/granite-4.0-1b, the checkpoint that carries the absolute threshold. COMPLETE, 0 assertion failures, 54,839 generated tokens at 73.6 tok/s. Bought three answers for 0.30 GPU-h. The competitor loads and renders our tool contract under its own chat template. The two surface forms are not interchangeable for it: 0.7795 composite under native_tools against 0.1841 under tools_text, where 299 of 378 completions are the bare string <tool_call> and nothing after it, which is a fact about the checkpoint and not about our parser. And it generates at a quarter of the reference checkpoint's rate on the same card at the same batch size, so its full pass was repriced at about 5 h and the task ceiling raised to 7 h rather than raising its batch size away from the reference it is compared against.
entries.note: Also the run that found the artifact bug properly. Five of eleven files logged as saved were absent from the artifact listing and from job download; the six present were exactly the six saved without type="evals". The type argument files a copy under eval-results metadata instead of the generic artifact store, and the CLI has no path to it. Every save in the eval task now saves untyped, so the scored per-item files and the run summary come back from here on.
